_comment: S624 — the agent eval's known-good score and the cases known to fail.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. In one session the eval went 42/45 -> 38/45 -> 9/45 and
nobody noticed until it was run again by hand, because a score printed to a
terminal and then scrolled away is not a baseline. Prompt edits are the
dangerous kind: they cannot be unit-tested, they degrade tool selection
silently, and their cost is invisible in a diff.
Update this file ONLY with a run that improved things, and say in the commit
which change moved which case. If a case moves from failing to passing,
remove it from knownFailures in the same commit.

notes.howThisWasReached: 45/45 across two paced blocks (21 tenant, 24 landlord/guest/prospect). Four of the six problems fixed to get here were GUARDS OR ASSERTIONS punishing correct behaviour, not agents being wrong.
notes.readItAsADiff: One seeded run is ONE DRAW. It makes a change comparable before and after, which is what regression detection needs. It is not a grade — a clean score is not proof the agents are good.
notes.doNotChunkAndCompare: The seed is per PROCESS, so a chunked run and a single run are not comparable to each other. Compare like with like.

pacing: AGENT_EVAL_PAUSE_MS, default 3000 — the host kernel-panicked twice under unpaced runs
